5
A student uses a cathode-ray oscilloscope (c.r.o.) to measure the period of a signal. She sets the
time-base of the c.r.o. to 5 ms cm–1 and observes the trace illustrated below. The trace has a
length of 10.0 cm.
10.0 cm
What is the period of the signal?
A
7.1 × 10–6
s
B
1.4 × 10–5
s
C
7.1 × 10–3
s
D
1.4 × 10–2
s

hints: Notice the horizontal scale: time-base $5 \text{ ms cm}^{-1}$ and total trace length $10.0 \text{ cm}$, so first work out the total time shown on the screen.
Count complete cycles across the $10.0 \text{ cm}$ trace: there are 4 peaks but only 3 troughs, so the trace contains $3.5$ full sine waves, not 3 or 4.
Connect the two numbers with $T = \text{total time} / \text{number of cycles}$ and convert milliseconds to seconds before comparing with the powers of ten.
walkthrough: Find the total time represented by the whole $10.0 \text{ cm}$ trace. Time-base means time per cm in the x-direction: $t_{total} = 10.0 \text{ cm} \times 5 \text{ ms cm}^{-1} = 50 \text{ ms}$.
Count how many full periods fill that time. One period is peak-to-peak or trough-to-trough. The diagram shows 4 peaks and 3 troughs, starting and ending mid-slope, which is $3.5$ complete cycles.
Use period = total time divided by number of cycles: $T = 50 \text{ ms} / 3.5$.
Calculate: $T \approx 14.3 \text{ ms}$. Convert to seconds: $14.3 \text{ ms} = 14.3 \times 10^{-3} \text{ s} \approx 1.4 \times 10^{-2} \text{ s}$.
This matches $1.4 \times 10^{-2} \text{ s}$. This is option D

A.explanation: Too small by a factor of 1000. It uses $7.1 \text{ ms}$ but writes it as $7.1 \times 10^{-6} \text{ s}$ instead of $10^{-3} \text{ s}$.

B.explanation: Too small by a factor of 1000. It uses about $14 \text{ ms}$ total divided correctly but writes milliseconds as $10^{-6} \text{ s}$ instead of $10^{-3} \text{ s}$.

C.explanation: Half the correct period. It divides the $50 \text{ ms}$ sweep time by about 7, treating peaks and troughs as full cycles instead of $3.5$ full cycles.

D.explanation: Correct. Total time $50 \text{ ms}$ divided by $3.5$ cycles gives about $14 \text{ ms} = 1.4 \times 10^{-2} \text{ s}$.
